articles.title: Marvel's VisionQuest Episode 7 Review: 'Immolation'
articles.summary: Full spoilers ahead for VisionQuest Episode 7! Paul Bettany may nominally be the star of VisionQuest, but we can all probably agree that this has largely been The James Spader Show up until now. Spader's gleefully acerbic Ultron has been the best and most pressing reason to follow the series.
body: "Immolation" opens with a WWII-era flashback, where we finally meet the elusive Phineas Horton in the flesh. And - surprise, surprise - he turns out to be played by Mr. Bettany. This is the first of several opportunities Bettany has to play a different character in Episode 7, and he doesn't waste it. There's such a palpable sense of haunted suffering emanating from Horton in this scene, and it nicely sets the tone for the rest of the episode.

From there, the show forces Vision to look inward and finally deal with all the emotions and memories he's been suppressing since he first climbed off that operating table at S.W.O.R.D. If VisionQuest is literally about the character undertaking a stereotypical vision quest, then this marks the point where he consumes a bunch of peyote and goes off in search of true enlightenment.
points: Paul Bettany may nominally be the star of VisionQuest, but we can all probably agree that this has largely been The James Spader Show up until now.

articles.title: James Bond Casting History: How Media Covered Past 007 Reveals
articles.summary: “Sean Connery, chosen to play Bond on the screen, had better be good.” November 3 marks the 65th anniversary of the announcement of Sean Connery’s casting as the big screen’s first James Bond – and it turns out people were complaining about Bond casting even back then.
body: I did a deep dive on Newspapers.com to see how the media covered the casting of James Bond, from Sean Connery through Daniel Craig. Relatively unknown actors faced tougher scrutiny than actors like Roger Moore and Pierce Brosnan who were known for playing Bond-like roles on TV shows.

One has to remember what a phenomenon James Bond was in the early 1960s. Ian Fleming’s novels were bestsellers and even President John F. Kennedy made his 007 fandom known. There had been much anticipation about James Bond finally getting the big screen treatment in Dr. No – Alfred Hitchcock and Cary Grant even eyed it at one point –so when it was announced that Scottish actor Sean Connery had won the role, the biggest response was: Who?
As you can see from some of the headlines below, Connery is branded an unknown – the last time he ever would be called that as he became a global superstar thanks to the franchise.
Until Daniel Craig inherited the role and started giving his legacy a run for its memory, Connery topped (nearly) every “who is the best Bond?” poll there was.
points: “Sean Connery, chosen to play Bond on the screen, had better be good.
November 3 marks the 65th anniversary of the announcement of Sean Connery’s casting as the big screen’s first James Bond – and it turns out people were complaining about Bond casting even back then.

articles.title: This Custom Xbox-Inside-An-Alligator Console Is Actually One Big Ad For GTA 6
articles.summary: Given that Sony holds the marketing rights for Grand Theft Auto 6, Microsoft has had to get creative to promote the open-world crime game for Xbox--and the company's latest effort in that department goes big.
body: Say Hello to the X-Bite, a playable Xbox Series X console that was designed to look like it was swallowed whole by one of Florida's millions of alligators. Microsoft only made one of these ornate consoles, and you have to win a contest to get it.

Microsoft's blog post doesn't mention GTA 6 or Rockstar Games, but Xbox marketing boss Josh Munsee said the system has "pure Miami vibes," and that's a pretty obvious reference to GTA 6 given the game takes place in a stand-in, Vice City, for the popular Florida city. The blog post says the winner of the console can play "some of the biggest games of the year" using it, and that's no doubt another nod to GTA 6.

"This November, Xbox is heading to Florida--home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe," Microsoft said in its announcement of the X-Bite.

The X-Bite is about five feet long, and the console itself sits inside the alligator, with the Nexus/Guide button illuminated through the gator's skin. The lucky winner will also get a custom Xbox controller with simulated bite marks on it.

articles.title: 007 First Light Gets Free Trial For Select PlayStation Plus Subscribers
articles.summary: Select PlayStation Plus subscribers can try 007 First Light for free via a new trial. 007 First Light is one of the biggest games of 2026, but you'd be forgiven for having missed it. It's been a busy year filled with a wide variety of awesome things to play.
body: This will allow you to play the game's prologue and some of Bond's training sections, which are actually quite fun and inventive for a video game tutorial. It's a great way to come to grips not only with how the game feels to play, but also the story and IO Interactive's take on Bond. If you like it, you can buy the game for 40% off, which brings it down to about $42.
007 First Light is one of the most well-reviewed games of 2026, with IGN giving it a 9 out of 10 and praising it for being a smart yet faithful evolution of the beloved spy franchise.

"Demonstrably obsessed with bringing the Bond fantasy to life in a way no game has ever managed before, developer IO Interactive has found a highly successful home for the more curated action-stealth formula of 2012’s Hitman: Absolution," reads an excerpt from our review. "Patiently paced, First Light is brimming with Bond’s trinity of gadgets, guns, and girls in a way that feels fresh but reverent, and never like parody."

articles.title: Get a 36V 500W Peak Adult Electric Bike for $210 Shipped During the AliExpress Early Black Friday Sale
articles.summary: With prices of electric bikes reaching an all-time low, it's time to retire that pedal-powered bike of yours. Nowadays you can find a decent ebike for well under $500 if you know where to look (hint: it's not necessarily Amazon).
body: The 5th Wheel AB17 bike is an adult electric bike featuring a 500W (700W peak) motor that can get up to speeds of 23mph. The 36V 375Wh lithium battery provides up to 25 miles on electric only mode and up to 45 miles on pedal-assist mode. The actual distance is dependent on other factors like your speed, terrain, elevation, and so forth. The frame is made of carbon steel so it's on the heavier side at about 50 pounds, but it also has a generous weight capacity of 265 pounds. The bike comes 85% preassembled and includes a 1 year warranty. It's also UL 2849 certified for safety.

There are other bikes out there that offer higher-quality components, a more powerful motor, better upgradeability, and/or domestic customer support, but only if you're willing to shell out hundreds or thousands of dollars more. The 5th Wheel AB17 bike is a perfectly respectable assisted ride that will satisfy most casual bikers at an unbeatable price. Frankly speaking, you have few other legitimate options if you're looking for a brand new adult ebike for under $300.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Shamans Are Protesting Class Changes After Being “Completely Ignored”
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever just received a massive batch of class-balance updates ahead of launch that have boosted power across the board, but one group of players isn't happy with the changes: Shamans.
body: Developer Blizzard recently released Forever's launch patch notes based on feedback and data accumulated during the beta, resulting in a power spike for all classes and major reworks for classes like Paladin and Rogue. Shamans, too, received some significant changes, most notably the removal of a key Elemental specialization ability, Lava Burst, along with any interactions other abilities had with it.

It's that change, and other changes to specialization-specific abilities like Restoration's Riptide and Enhancement's Maelstrom Weapon, that have resulted in the WoW Classic Shaman Discord going into lockdown in protest. The entire server, which has around 80,000 members, has been made read-only, with a message declaring the reason for why it took what it described as such a "drastic measure."

"Community feedback gets completely ignored and class fantasies are getting destroyed," the server declared. "With this we intend to give them [Blizzard] a sign and show them that the community is not [happy] with how they approached our beloved class. Give us back our class and spec identities and fantasies."
points: World of Warcraft: Forever just received a massive batch of class-balance updates ahead of launch that have boosted power across the board, but one group of players isn't happy with the changes…

articles.title: WoW: Forever Won’t Get More Class Balance Changes Any Time Soon
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is gearing up for launch with some major class balance changes, but don't expect any more for at least a month. As detailed in Forever's launch patch notes, Blizzard is making some dramatic class changes, including major reworks to Rogue and Paladin talents, in time for…
body: However, don't expect additional changes in the near future. Blizzard said it won't be making significant balance changes until sometime next month.

"With the exception of bugs and serious outliers, we don't plan on making big tuning changes between now and the opening of the raids next month," Blizzard wrote in its patch notes. "Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data."
Forever's three launch raids will open December 9, meaning there will be a little over a month without class changes. But launch and its subsequent months will just be the beginning, Blizzard said.

"This is all merely a starting point for the classes in Forever, which will continue over the course of the months and years ahead just as they did following the original launch in 2004," Blizzard said.

articles.title: The Wendy’s JRPG Is a Searing Anti-Capitalist Screed About Humans Making Real Art
articles.summary: Over the past year, Wendy’s — yes, the same Wendy’s known for its square burgers, thick milkshakes, and unlikely stewardship of a mid-tier donut chain — has made waves through a series of unconventional creative partnerships.
body: The resistance against the AI art apocalypse is being televised in a marketing campaign about burgers.

The buzziest Wendy’s-affiliated project was the post-hardcore EP Songs to Listen to in a Wendy’s Parking Lot, which featured six tracks written by musicians from bands with legit emo cred, like Anberlin, Blessthefall, Silverstein, and Winona Fighter. Look, I am as sorry as you are to hand anything to Big Corporate, but all six tracks are straight bangers. (Just listen to “ She Said She Didn’t Want Fries ” and try to tell me you didn’t have that on repeat in a Wendy’s parking lot in 2008.) On the heels of that album release is the classic JRPG riff WendyQuest: Legend of the Four Corner Stones. Like Songs to Listen to, it boasts a similar unmistakable authenticity.
WendyQuest started as many projects in the indie gaming world do: funding. Or, rather, a lack thereof.

articles.title: Bethesda's associate art director really did try to fit 7,000 actual steps into Skyrim's 7,000 Steps: 'I take no responsibility for the Frost Troll'
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: When the Greybeards invite you to High Hrothgar in Skyrim, you have to climb a mountain to reach them. There's a messenger called Klimmek waiting in the village of Ivarstead at the bottom to warn you what an arduous journey this is going to be. To get to the top of the Throat of the World, he says, you have to work your way up The 7,000 Steps.

It's well-documented that there aren't actually 7,000 steps carved into the side of the mountain. Some of them are buried under the snow, making an exact count impossible, but the actual number is closer to 700. And even if you argue that The 7,000 Steps refers to the number of footsteps it takes to ascend the mountain, according to the dedicated researchers at the Ultimate Elder Scrolls Portal it only takes "approximately 2,400 footsteps" to get there.

As part of Bethesda's 40th anniversary, which included the reveal of The Elder Scrolls 6's subtitle, the studio reminisced about their previous work, which is how we know they really did try to get 7,000 steps into the side of the mountain.

articles.title: Ubisoft Makes Bid to Purchase Xbox Studio on the Brink of Closure
articles.summary: Microsoft intends to divest from Dishonored and Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Studios as part of its mass layoffs at Xbox and other Microsoft divisions. Because Arkane is based in Lyon, France, Xbox has had to adhere to French labor laws, and was mandated to search for a potential buyer for…
body: Assassin's Creed maker Ubisoft has reportedly made an offer for Arkane, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday. Ubisoft is one of at least three companies to submit a bid for Arkane. According to Bloomberg, Xbox is also considering selling Arkane to the studio's management.

The future of Arkane looked in doubt last month as negotiations for a redundancy plan for potentially laid-off employees were reportedly not going well ahead of a Nov. 13 deadline. That deadline for Arkane to find a new home was extended, and Xbox is "exploring options" for what to do with Arkane ahead of its December deadline, Bloomberg said. Xbox has not accepted any offer at this time.
Marvel's Blade was announced almost three years ago at the 2023 The Game Awards. Arkane has been quiet about it since, and its internal ship date was delayed until late 2027.

If Arkane avoids being shut down by Microsoft and gets sold elsewhere, it will likely be able to wrap up development on its game starring The Daywalker. According to Bloomberg, Blade is "expected to be released within the next year or two."

articles.title: Valve admits it's 'running behind' on approving Steam games because it has to keep re-reviewing them, which surely has nothing to do with AI
articles.summary: A new kind of Steam problem has emerged: Games keep missing their release dates because Valve can't keep up with approving them. Several frustrated indie devs have publicly posted about the limbo status of their finished games in the past week—including the developers of Food Devils, Wheel Make It…
body: In the case of Cubic Earth, developer structmira hasn't been able to contact Valve and has no choice but to wait. "Our game's trailer amassed more than 60,000 views on YouTube, and we had more than 6,000 wishlists," the developer told PC Gamer over email. "Now, our Steam Community page is rapidly filling with player complaints, and we've lost all momentum."

Valve commented on the backlog today in the form of a Steamworks update aimed at helping developers pass the preview process. In it, the company admitted that it's "running a little behind" with wait times that are up to double the usual.

"We aim to test every game build in a timely manner, typically within 3-5 days. However, we're running a little behind right now and taking up to 12 business days," Valve's FAQ reads. "Much of that delay is due to having to re-review games, which isn't great for you or for us."

articles.title: Ubisoft reportedly wants to buy Arkane from Xbox
articles.summary: A new report from Bloomberg says Dishonored developer Arkane might not be as doomed as it appeared last month, as multiple companies have made offers to acquire the studio.
body: Citing "people familiar with the negotiations," the Bloomberg report says Ubisoft is among Arkane's suitors, as are at least two other unnamed gaming companies. Xbox has also considered selling the studio to its own management, effectively making it independent, although whether that option is still on the table isn't clear.

Despite producing an enviable slate of acclaimed immersive sims over the years (until it was compelled by senior leadership to do otherwise ), Arkane fell victim to the Xbox "reset" in July that saw thousands of employees laid off (with more still awaiting their fates) and four studios cast adrift. Arkane avoided being the fifth, reportedly thanks to France's "Florange Law" that compelled Xbox to search for a buyer before pulling the plug.
